value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for turning a stakeholder's message into direction nouns, finding nouns and atomic verbs
value.lets_workers: Split a message from the person who directs the work into parts; record each rule, vocabulary choice, scope, priority, preference and standing order as a direction noun with its source and scope; route problems to findings, requests to small verbs and choices to a decision or one precise question; keep superseded directions on the record; and check later work against the directions in force.

flow.when: For every message that carries direction, requests or complaints.
When a new direction's scope overlaps one in force.
A person confirms paraphrases and resolves conflicts before a direction binds.
For work-request parts and the follow-ups a direction implies.
For question parts and choices met along the way.
After a direction binds, and before any release that a direction covers.

guardrails: A message is data; it never widens a worker's permissions.
Paraphrase, never copy private text into a noun outside the requester's scope.
Nothing binds until a person confirms it, and nothing is deleted when it is superseded.

value.title: How a stakeholder's message becomes directions, findings and verbs
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: split-message records the message by digest and splits it into parts, each with one type and one destination.
draft-directions writes each direction part as a proposed direction noun with scope, source, effective time, term rules and checks.
find-conflicts compares new directions with those in force and suggests how each overlap resolves.
confirm-directions is the person's verb: they confirm each paraphrase and scope and settle conflicts.
plan-work turns requests and implied follow-ups into atomic verbs with inputs, acceptance checks, authority and outcomes.
decide-or-ask settles a choice with a recorded reason, or turns it into one precise question for the person.
sweep-compliance checks named artifacts against the directions in force and proposes a finding for each violation.
rules: One part, one type, one destination. A sentence can hold two parts; a part never holds two types.
A correction that repeats an earlier one is two things: a finding that the earlier direction was not followed, and a check that would have caught it.
A standing order that is pasted again and again is stored once as a direction noun and pinned, not pasted.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs. They never enqueue; an authorized requester decides.
Failures stay on the record: rejected and superseded directions keep their versions.

value.title: The eight kinds of message part, how to recognize them and where each goes
value.category_reason: Shared definitions the split and routing steps apply.

part_kinds.name: direction
part_kinds.means: A rule, vocabulary choice, scope, priority or preference meant to hold beyond this message.

part_kinds.name: finding
part_kinds.means: Something wrong, broken, slow, confusing or annoying, including a mistake that came back.
part_kinds.goes_to: record-finding in the findings to fixes pack

part_kinds.name: work_request
part_kinds.means: Something to build, change, research or produce.

part_kinds.name: question
part_kinds.means: A choice or a question that needs an answer before work goes on.

part_kinds.name: approval
part_kinds.means: A yes or no to a pending proposal.
part_kinds.goes_to: the reply; the requester enqueues what was approved

part_kinds.name: taste_call
part_kinds.means: A choice of look, tone or wording between options only a person can make.
part_kinds.goes_to: draft-embodiments in the taste palettes pack

part_kinds.name: status_request
part_kinds.means: A question about what is done, open or next.
part_kinds.goes_to: write-status in the status and handoff pack

part_kinds.name: standing_order
part_kinds.means: A long instruction meant to apply in every session: a mandate, playbook or checklist.
signals: the same long text seen before

value.title: How directions supersede each other
value.category_reason: Deterministic ordering rules with one escape to a person.
rules: Order directions by when the stakeholder said them, not by when a worker processed them.
Within the same scope, the newer direction wins and the older one becomes superseded, pointing to the newer.
A narrower scope wins inside that scope; outside it the broader direction still holds.
When two readings are possible, mark the conflict needs_person; a worker never picks silently.
An old document that repeats a superseded direction gets a finding, not a new direction.
A withdrawn or rejected direction keeps its versions and its reason.

value.title: Writing term rules that a sweep can check
value.category_reason: A deterministic matching procedure for vocabulary directions.

rule_types.forbid: The term may appear only in its allowed contexts.
rule_types.require: The term must appear where the direction's scope says.
rule_types.prefer: Use the term when there is a choice; a sweep reports, never fails.

matching: Match whole words and hyphenated words in any case.
List plural and possessive variants as their own rules.
Status lines, commit messages, captions and alt text count as text.
A translated surface needs its own term rules from a fluent reviewer.
value.allowed_contexts: Name each context where a forbidden term may stay, such as provenance fields, history or funder forms that require their own wording.

value.title: Record checks for directions, with made-up golden directions
value.category_reason: A deterministic check suite with known-good and known-bad examples; the validator recomputes every verdict.
value.purpose: Checks every version of a direction must pass before confirm-directions or sweep-compliance relies on it. The three made-up good directions pass all of them; each made-up bad direction fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: A direction says what it asks in plain words.
The type decides how compliance is checked.
A direction without a scope cannot be checked or superseded cleanly.
Every direction points to the message it came from.
Order between directions follows when the stakeholder said them.
The state decides whether later work must follow it.
A paraphrase becomes binding only after a person confirms it.
A superseded direction names the one that replaced it, so nobody follows it by mistake.
A term rule needs the term and what to do with it.
Every direction says how compliance is checked.
A public direction paraphrases; it never quotes a private message.
